label.en: ⚠️ Classic ACT Traps: Percents, Ratios & Number Properties

body.en:
• Percent Change Base Value: Always divide the difference by the original starting value, never the new value: \( \text{Percent Change} = \frac{\text{New} - \text{Old}}{\text{Old}} \times 100\% \).
  • Successive Percentage Changes Do Not Add: A 20% discount followed by a 10% discount is NOT a 30% discount. The total multiplier is \( 0.80 \times 0.90 = 0.72 \), meaning an effective 28% total discount.
  • Ratio Parts vs. Whole: If boys to girls is \( 3:5 \), boys represent \( \frac{3}{3+5} = \frac{3}{8} \) of the total students, NOT \( \frac{3}{5} \). Always add ratio terms to find total parts.
  • Number Property Facts: \( 2 \) is the only even prime number; \( 1 \) is neither prime nor composite; \( 0 \) is an even integer (neither positive nor negative).

question.en: A jacket costs $120 after a 25% discount. What was the original price?
A merchant buys a gadget for $50, marks it up by 40%, and later sells it at a 20% discount off the marked price. What was the final selling price and the merchant's net profit?

solution.en: Marked price: \(50 \times 1.40 = \$70\). Sale price after 20% discount: \(70 \times 0.80 = \$56\). Net profit: \(56 - 50 = \$6\).
